One neuron stands out: L16 n3729. Its last-prompt activation correlates +0.71 with choosing R0, the highest correlation in layers 12–20. Its down_proj column has cosine −0.38 with the R1-minus-R0 direction, so when it fires it writes toward R0. Every other top-correlated neuron has a near-orthogonal column (|cos| ≤ 0.08), so they only reflect the regime without writing it.

I had scaled n3729 up in the x3/x6 edits, believing it pushed toward R1. Its sign must be checked: GeGLU activations can be negative, and amplifying a neuron that carries both signs does different things on different prompts.

I'll print n3729's mean, standard deviation and fraction-positive at the last prompt token for R0 and R1 prompts. I'll print the same for its mean over answer tokens, to see whether it also acts during generation.

If it is positive and larger on R0 prompts, zeroing it (or reversing it) is a clean candidate edit that removes the R0 push. If it changes sign between regimes, the x3 result has a different explanation and I'll need to rethink.

n3729 is a prompt-end neuron. At the last prompt token it is always positive and among the three most active neurons in layer 16 by mean |activation|: 2.09 on R0 prompts and 1.31 on R1 prompts. Over answer tokens it is essentially zero (|mean| ≤ 0.02). Its column writes toward R0, so it is a positive "go terse" push, stronger on prompts that end up in R0.

Because it is nearly silent during generation, zeroing its down_proj column should change little beyond the regime choice at the end of the prompt. That makes it a much cleaner lever than the column scaling. The earlier x3/x6 edits amplified this neuron together with n180 and n3621, so their effects were mixed and are not a guide to this one.

I'll drop the current edits and save a single one: model.layers.16.mlp.down_proj column 3729 set to zero, from the original weights. I'll test it with a paired "both" pass on DEV[512:768].

How to read the result:
- **Lever works:** problems shift from R0 to R1 with a paired accuracy gain. That would show this neuron holds the model in the weak mode.
- **Fails:** a shift with no gain, or more loops eating the gain, means the regime lever is capped by loops.

The edit is saved: only model.layers.16.mlp.down_proj, with column 3729 set to zero from the original weights. I'm running the paired generation on DEV[512:768].

I'll compare this result with pass 5 (x3 on the same problems, +0.4 ± 2.3, cuts 31→46). A gain of about +3 or more with a regime shift toward R1 supports the lever. A shift with flat accuracy and rising cuts means loops cap it.

Zeroing n3729 gave +1.2 ± 1.9 points on DEV[512:768], with 13 answers going wrong to right and 10 right to wrong. Answers got longer (330 vs 294 tokens) and cuts rose from 31 to 37. That is the same pattern as x3: a small, non-significant gain partly eaten by loops.

I'll count regimes and per-regime accuracy and cut rates in both files, to see how many problems actually switched and how the switched ones fared. If most problems moved to R1 but the switched ones loop more often than native R1 answers, the regime lever is capped by the loop failure. Removing that cap would need its own mechanism.
